# Our meeting notes got read once we cut them to a page

Nobody read the notes from our weekly meeting. I counted the views in the shared folder for three months, and the average set of notes was opened by 1.4 people. Leave out the person who wrote them and it was close to nobody.

## They were too long

I printed last month's notes, and one meeting came to eleven pages. We had been writing down what each person said, in order, so the decisions only showed up in the last paragraph. If you opened the file to find out what we had agreed, you had to read all of it. The follow-ups just said "look into it", with no name and no date.

## What we changed

Since April the decisions go in the first three lines. Every follow-up gets a name and a date. We stopped writing down who said what, and only keep a line when someone disagrees, with their reason. The note taker changes every week. I wrote the first two, and from the third week Priya, who joined in March, took her turn.

## What happened

The four sets of notes in May averaged one page. They were opened by 5.2 people on average. Last week someone who had read the notes reminded a colleague that a follow-up was overdue. Once there is a date on it, people other than the owner notice when it slips.

Next month we will paste the first three lines straight into the team channel and see whether anyone still opens the file.
